summary: Twelve comment-endorsed developer tools, learning resources, services, and practical products from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Merge AI Gateway
items.source_story_title: So you want to use OpenRouter?
items.summary: A unified AI-model gateway that quickly adds providers and models.
items.why_included: A current user praised its usefulness, fast model additions, and responsive support.
items.evidence: The commenter reported positive ongoing use and responsive support.

evidence_sources.author: vinhnx
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using Merge AI Gateway and it's been useful so far. They tend to add new models quickly, and support has been responsive.

items.name: Trace
items.source_story_title: RTK reports token savings, but our cost benchmarks disagree
items.summary: A tree-sitter tool that builds compact outlines of files and directories.
items.why_included: A user employs Trace to save agent time and improve codebase orientation.
items.evidence: The commenter uses tree-sitter outlines because models struggle to obtain an overview.

evidence_sources.author: monneyboi
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use treesitter to build outlines of files and directories:

items.name: Magit
items.source_story_title: Working with Git Worktrees in Magit
items.summary: An Emacs Git interface with integrated worktree management.
items.why_included: An AI-agent worktree user loved Magit and planned to adopt its worktree support.
items.evidence: The commenter praised Magit's worktree handling and intended to use it immediately.

evidence_sources.author: brabel
evidence_sources.excerpt: And I love Magit but didn’t know it handles git worktrees so well!

items.name: Git Repo Manager
items.source_story_title: Working with Git Worktrees in Magit
items.summary: A command-line tool for managing repositories and Git worktrees.
items.why_included: A current user said its grm command makes worktree administration easier.
items.evidence: The commenter uses grm specifically to simplify worktree administration.

evidence_sources.author: prima-facie
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use grm when I need worktrees, which makes admin a bit easier;

items.name: godot-rust
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Godot and Rust based multiplexer (terminal panes and more)
items.summary: Rust language bindings for building games and applications with Godot 4.
items.why_included: A team reported extensive use, strong support, and unqualified praise.
items.evidence: The commenter described extensive first-hand use and praised the bindings' support.

evidence_sources.author: TkTech
evidence_sources.excerpt: godot-rust is a extremely well supported - we've used it extensively and have nothing but praise.

items.name: earlyoom
items.source_story_title: Stop making swap partitions—use swap files instead
items.summary: A Linux daemon that kills processes before severe out-of-memory lockups.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended it for more aggressive out-of-memory handling.
items.evidence: The recommendation presented earlyoom as a way to trigger OOM killing sooner.

evidence_sources.author: negrel
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend using the earlyoom if you want more aggresive oom kill:

items.name: HN Sans AI
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: Can we please limit the AI news flood?
items.summary: A Hacker News view that filters AI-related stories from the feed.
items.why_included: A commenter uses it when they need a break from peak AI hype.
items.evidence: The commenter identified HN Sans AI as their practical break from AI-heavy news.

evidence_sources.author: leonheld
evidence_sources.excerpt: HN is a reflection of the industry and we're at peak hype-cycle at the moment. I use this when I need a break

items.name: Snap!
items.source_story_title: Λ Snap – An inviting programming language for kids and adults for CS study
items.summary: A browser-based visual programming language combining blocks with Scheme's power.
items.why_included: An experienced educator strongly endorsed Snap! for teaching Scheme concepts to children.
items.evidence: The commenter called themselves a huge fan and praised Snap!'s mix of visual blocks and Scheme.

evidence_sources.author: DonHopkins
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'm also a huge fan of Snap!, which has all the advantages of Logo (Lisp without parenthesis) and Scratch / eToys / Squeak / App Inventor family of block based visual programming languages, but all the power of Scheme.

items.name: Logo
items.summary: A beginner-friendly programming language built around procedures, recursion, and turtle graphics.
items.why_included: A former learner and PhD instructor praised Logo for making programming concepts tangible.
items.evidence: The commenter delighted in learning Logo and found it helped students internalize programming.

evidence_sources.author: yogsototh
evidence_sources.excerpt: I myself learned programming with logo, at my school when I was 8 or 10. And it was a delight, I am so grateful it existed.

items.name: 3Blue1Brown phase-kickback animation
items.summary: A short visual explanation of phase kickback in electromagnetic waves.
items.why_included: A commenter singled it out as a beautiful animation for a difficult concept.
items.evidence: The commenter praised the animation as a clear visual treatment of phase kickback.

evidence_sources.author: prathje
evidence_sources.excerpt: 3Blue1Brown has a beautiful animation for this phase kickback here:

items.name: YouTube Premium
items.source_story_title: I spent $220 on Google app ads and 60% of the installs were robots
items.summary: YouTube's paid plan for ad-free viewing, downloads, and background playback.
items.why_included: A paying user reported strong value while noting that creators receive more per view.
items.evidence: The commenter described substantial personal return on the subscription price.

evidence_sources.author: xp84
evidence_sources.excerpt: I guess I'm just saying I see a ton of ROI on the $16.

items.name: IKEA KNAGGLIG
items.source_story_title: Don't let anyone take away your big box of cables
items.summary: A small pine storage crate sized for sorting household cable collections.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended the small boxes for their looks and useful size.
items.evidence: The commenter recommended KNAGGLIG boxes as attractive, appropriately sized cable storage.

evidence_sources.author: MrBuddyCasino
evidence_sources.excerpt: I can recommend the small Ikea Knagglig boxes, they look nice and have the right size.
